audit: The recipe-kit analogy explains reuse and selective opening but can blur instruction loading with executable authority. Lesson A splits those two requests and gives each its own gate, allowing a reader to predict why opening a reviewed refund procedure is different from running its financial step. Lesson B examines a release manifest with one unresolved dependency range. Its failed check shows exactly why a past invocation cannot be reproduced until versions and hashes are pinned. Together these examples preserve the distinction between the book's local packaging convention and a runtime-specific format, without claiming that signed content or a manifest supplies permission.

lessons.title: Opening the recipe is not cooking the refund
lessons.intro: A caller selects refund kit v2.3.0. The host distinguishes loading its instructions from invoking a financial step inside its procedure.

data.root: Requested use of refund kit v2.3.0

branches.question: Approved package and loading scope valid?

no.label: No execution; deny or seek valid review

read: The root separates two operations involving the same package.
A loaded instruction file adds know-how to context.
Financial execution needs independent authority and an approved exact effect.
lessons.question: If the package is signed by its author, may its script grant itself refunds:execute?
lessons.answer: No. A signature establishes package provenance, not execution authority. The host supplies permitted capabilities, and the service enforces the effect contract. A script included in an approved kit remains subject to those controls.
lessons.takeaway: Reusable procedure knowledge does not amplify the caller's privileges.
lessons.assumption: Fictional two-operation scope; execution also needs fresh preconditions, budgets and effect identity. The recipe analogy does not guarantee repeatable model behavior.

lessons.anchor: Discovery, versioning, trust and access control
lessons.title: Resolve the recipe's dependencies before release
lessons.intro: A refund skill release has a compatibility range for one tool but no recorded resolution. The other dependency is pinned.

data.name: Refund kit release candidate

checks.label: Exact dependencies
checks.detail: get_order has no resolved version or hash

data.result: Resolve, pin and test the complete assembly first

read: The range expresses compatibility, not the artifact used by a run.
The pinned payment tool can be identified without rerunning resolution.
Release tests must target the same assembly the runtime records.
lessons.question: If get_order 2.2.0 is published tomorrow, should a pending approved run silently adopt it?
lessons.answer: No. The run continues under its exact pinned assembly or follows an explicit recorded migration policy. Re-resolving a mutable range during continuation can alter the implementation after review and make prior behavior difficult to reproduce.
lessons.takeaway: Compatibility ranges guide resolution; exact versions and hashes explain execution.
lessons.assumption: Fictional local manifest convention, not an interoperable file-format claim. Dependency pinning improves traceability without guaranteeing behavior or live-data freshness.
